evidence.note: 'The drop is a diversion problem, not a fleet or staffing one' is an 'X, not Y' antithesis, which the profile bans in body copy.
'On-time departures fell from 86% to 81% in Q3, and retiming the diverted routes is the Q4 test' joins a finding and a plan in an 'X, and Y' pair, the construction the profile rejected for titles.

'Retiming 12 and 14 Cross-town for the diversion is the Q4 test, checked at the end of January' frames a plan as 'the Q4 test' instead of stating a finding; s-2 tile 3 heading 'Retime routes 12 and 14 Cross-town...' is imperative.
'Routes 12 and 14 Cross-town account for almost all of the network's fall. The other six routes' median moved by under 1 point.' is finding-first and carries the evidence number, as the profile asks.
Plain cause and consequence: a fleet or staffing shortfall would cut recovery time on every route, so the Q3 drop points to the diversion.
Most titles (s-1, s-3, s-4, s-5, s-6, s-7) are specific declarative findings, one sentence with no trailing full stop and no hooks or wordplay.
The driver quote is verbatim under a neutral label ('Driver, 12 Cross-town') with a cite, and there is no editorialising in the tile.
Three specific, grounded open questions (running time at the school run, the vacancies-vs-closures test, lost mileage beside the target), matching the profile's prompt rule.

rationale: Most of the copy follows the profile: titles state findings, overlays explain cause and consequence with numbers, and the quote and prompts follow their rules. But there are several lapses the presenter would rewrite: an 'X, not Y' antithesis on s-2, an 'X, and Y' title on s-2, and 'the Q4 test' framing with an imperative heading on s-2 and s-8. That matches level 3.
